title: Coefficient compatibility of the chosen compact-support Frobenius transport
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a_X:X\to s$. Fix a compactification $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{r_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use its base change $c=(j,r)$ and the specified compactification-relative Frobenius exchange [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] at every coefficient stage.

For $F=E,M$ and $Z=X,s$, use the raw rationalized category $\mathcal C_F(Z)=D^b_c(Z,\mathcal O_F)[1/\varpi_F]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with no idempotent completion. Let $T_Z:\mathcal C_E(Z)\to\mathcal C_M(Z)$ be integral completed scalar extension followed by rationalization. Write $V=-\otimes_E M:D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(M)$ for scalar extension of module complexes. Let $G_F=Lg_{X,F}^*$ and $H_F=Lg_{s,F}^*$ be geometric-Frobenius pullbacks [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $A_F=Ra^c_{X!,F}:\mathcal C_F(X)\to\mathcal C_F(s)$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and $B_F=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,F}:\mathcal C_F(s)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $C_F=B_FA_F$. Let $t_{F,K}:C_FK\to C_FG_FK$ be the actual transport [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport].

For $K\in\mathcal C_E(X)$ use $d_K:T_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_MT_XK$, the rationalization of the canonical pullback comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with the specified simultaneous-diagram normalization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Let $\rho_K:T_sA_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}A_MT_XK$ be the compact-support operation comparison [lem-fix-operation-reduction] for the fixed $c$. Let $v_N:VB_EN\xrightarrow{\sim}B_MT_sN$ be the inverse of the rational sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Define $b_K=B_M(\rho_K)v_{A_EK}:VC_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}C_MT_XK$. Then in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(M)$,
$$C_M(d_K)b_{G_EK}V(t_{E,K})=t_{M,T_XK}b_K.$$
The equation is natural in $K$ and compatible with identity and successive finite field extensions under the specified scalar associators. Its exchange compatibility holds already for the specified maps on strict semilinear coefficient diagrams before realization, and therefore for their integral realizations and rationalizations. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on reductions is imposed. The same canonical pullback scalar comparisons commute with the canonical composition identifications for successive Frobenius pullbacks.

proof.text: Fix the compactification in the statement. Write $P_F=Rr_{*,F}$, $J_F=j_{!,F}$ and $U_F=Lg_{\overline X,F}^*$, so $A_F=P_FJ_F$. Use the same notation on integral models. The Frobenius squares for $r_0,j_0,a_{X_0}$ use the automorphisms induced on the factor $k$, not morphisms over $k$. They are Cartesian by [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. Pullback by these automorphisms preserves integral bounded constructible objects [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Compact support for $a_X$ and for $j$ has integral bounded constructible output [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible]; for $j$ its compactification is $j$ followed by the identity of $\overline X$, so this gives the domain of $J_F$. The proper $r$ is a finite-type $k$-morphism, so [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] gives the domain of $P_F$. Thus all integral comparisons used below apply to $K$, $G_EK$, $J_EK$ and their images. Rationalization uses exactly these objects.

source.place: Steps 2-4, bounded integral operation domains and passage to the raw field stages; expanded for the chosen Frobenius square.

proof.text: Work first with whole coefficient diagrams. On each corner $Z$, use strict semilinear systems of $(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_Z$-modules as in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], with the simultaneous derived pullbacks, proper direct images, open extensions and adjunction maps specified there. Coefficient extension is derived, computed on K-flat models; it is not assumed exact between finite quotient rings. The actual quotient maps and scalar/pullback chain maps are the ones of [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence], which commute with transitions even for ramified $E\subset M$. In these models the proper exchange is the specified mate, and the open exchange is the specified open-adjunction map. Use the coefficient operation comparisons and their preservation of units, counits and tensor associativity from [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. This chooses the maps being compared before applying any evaluation or inverse limit; equality after separate finite evaluations will not be used to infer equality of system maps.

source.place: Step 2, compatible coefficient constructions, and Step 3, passage to the adic stage; the strict model of def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange specifies this passage.

proof.text:
Let $a_{f,L}:T Lf_E^*L\to Lf_M^*TL$ denote the pullback coefficient comparison on the relevant corners. By [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], for composable $h,k$ its simultaneous-diagram normalization satisfies
$$Lh_M^*(a_{k,L})a_{h,Lk_E^*L}T(c^E_{h,k,L})=c^M_{h,k,TL}a_{kh,L}.$$
Apply this to the two composites $r g_{\overline X}=g_s r$. Identifying those composites by that equality of scheme maps gives precisely the pull-comparison cube for the proper Frobenius square. This checks the square-identification factor as well as the two pullback comparisons; naturality of a single pullback comparison alone would not do so. The asserted equations hold for whole quotient diagrams, and the canonical comparisons in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] are the realizations of these specified families.

proof.text:
For the proper factor let $u_L:T_sP_EL\to P_MT_{\overline X}L$ be its coefficient comparison, and $e^r_F:H_FP_F\to P_FU_F$ its Frobenius exchange. The mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] writes this exchange as $R(H\varepsilon)\circ R(\theta)\circ\eta$: the unit, the pullback-square identification, and the counit. In the coefficient cube take the four adjunctions to be $Lr_F^*\dashv P_F$, one at each vertical copy of the square, for $F=E,M$. The two horizontal comparisons are $a_{g_s}$ and $a_{g_{\overline X}}$; the two push comparisons are $u$. The specified $u$ is the mate of $a_r^{-1}$: $u_L=P_M(T_{\overline X}\varepsilon_{E,L})P_M(a_{r,P_EL}^{-1})\eta_{M,T_sP_EL}$. The preservation of actual units and counits in [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identifies this formula with the operation comparison, so both counit mate equations hold. The pull cube is Step 3. Thus every hypothesis of the general eight-category [lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates] is met, including invertibility of the pull coefficient comparisons, and it gives
$$P_M(a_{g_{\overline X},L})u_{U_EL}T_s(e^r_E(L))=e^r_M(T_{\overline X}L)H_M(u_L)a_{g_s,P_EL}.$$
This is the comparison of the specified proper exchange maps, without assuming the exchanges themselves invertible.

proof.text:
For the open factor put $z_K:T_{\overline X}J_EK\to J_MT_XK$. This is the canonical tensor/open-extension comparison: on the ringed slice site it is the inverse of the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. The small pro-etale slice identification is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. For the derived version use K-flat representatives: $J$ preserves K-flatness because the displayed tensor identity identifies $J(P)\otimes Q$ with $J(P\otimes j^*Q)$, acyclic for acyclic $Q$, as restriction and $J$ are exact on these models [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For completed coefficients use the canonical finite-free tensor/completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]; it identifies this map with the same coefficient-system construction. Write $o_F:U_FJ_F\to J_FG_F$ for the specified open exchange. On the simultaneous models [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], its inverse is the open-adjunction map whose restriction is the identity, as normalized in [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. Take the two composites comparing its coefficient extensions and transpose under $J_M\dashv j^*$. Their restrictions are both the identity after the pull-comparison cube for $j g_X=g_{\overline X}j$ (Step 3's composition equation, now for $j$). Preservation of the adjunction maps gives equal transposes; the mate bijection gives equal arrows. Inverting this identity gives
$$J_M(a_{g_X,K})z_{G_EK}T_{\overline X}(o_E(K))=o_M(T_XK)U_M(z_K)a_{g_{\overline X},J_EK}.$$
The construction and equality take place on whole coefficient diagrams.

proof.text:
Write $e_F=P_F(o_F)e^r_F$ for the compactification-relative exchange [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] and $\rho_K=P_M(z_K)u_{J_EK}$. This is the compact-support comparison for $A_F=P_FJ_F$ supplied by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Substitute the two equations of Steps 4-5 in this expression. Naturality of $u$ with respect to $o_E(K)$ moves it past $T(o_E(K))$; naturality of $e^r_M$ with respect to $z_K$ moves $P_MU_M(z_K)$ to $H_MP_M(z_K)$. The remaining adjacent factors are exactly $\rho_{G_EK}$ and $H_M(\rho_K)$. Hence
$$A_M(a_{g_X,K})\rho_{G_EK}T_s(e_E(K))=e_M(T_XK)H_M(\rho_K)a_{g_s,A_EK}.$$
This is the exchange square, obtained by pasting the proper and open squares with their specified comparison maps.

proof.text: Apply exact restriction to completed coefficients and the derived-limit functor on strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to Step 6. The simultaneous section models preserve the specified constructions and coherence homotopies [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Thus this is an equality of maps of diagrams to which a functor is applied, not a claim that finite reductions detect arbitrary morphisms. The comparison maps $\alpha_!,\beta_!$ in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] identify the resulting arrows with the defined integral exchange $\beta_!R\lim(e^c)\alpha_!$. The operation comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify the other arrows with the defined integral $a$ and $\rho$. Conjugating by these identifications gives exactly Step 6 at the integral level. Apply scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; it preserves composition and equality, and every rational object has an integral representative. The resulting equation holds in $\mathcal C_M(s)$ for all rational $K$, with $a_{g_X,K}=d_K$. No finite-level compact-support coefficient-change theorem with a finite-Tor hypothesis was applied.

source.place: Steps 3-4, integral realization followed by rationalization; the morphisms being realized are fixed before this passage.

proof.text:
For $N\in\mathcal C_E(s)$ put $a_{s,N}=a_{g_s,N}$ and use $v_N:VB_EN\to B_MT_sN$ in the statement. The rational sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and the definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] give this isomorphism between module complexes. The scalar-extension clause of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] (2), with the actual point transport of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], is the well-typed identity
$$B_M(a_{s,N})v_{H_EN}V(\iota_{E,N})=\iota_{M,T_sN}v_N.$$
Here both sides start at $VB_EN$ and end at $B_MH_MT_sN$. This uses the point-transport compatibility explicitly asserted there; it does not infer that assertion from naturality in a fixed coefficient category.

proof.text:
Now expand $t_{F,K}=B_F(e_F(K))\iota_{F,A_FK}$ using [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Put $N=A_EK$ and $N'=A_EG_EK$. Naturality of $v$ on $e_E(K)$, Step 7, Step 8, and then naturality of $\iota_M$ on $\rho_K$ give, in that order,
$$\begin{aligned}
C_M(d_K)b_{G_EK}V(t_{E,K})
&=B_M(A_M(d_K)\rho_{G_EK}T_s(e_E(K)))v_{H_EN}V(\iota_{E,N})\\
&=B_M(e_M(T_XK))B_M(H_M(\rho_K))B_M(a_{s,N})v_{H_EN}V(\iota_{E,N})\\
&=B_M(e_M(T_XK))B_M(H_M(\rho_K))\iota_{M,T_sN}v_N\\
&=B_M(e_M(T_XK))\iota_{M,A_MT_XK}B_M(\rho_K)v_N\\
&=t_{M,T_XK}b_K.
\end{aligned}$$
All arrows lie in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(M)$; the input is $VC_EK$ and the output is $C_MG_MT_XK$. This proves the displayed equation rather than identifying an unspecified transport with it.

proof.text: Every factor in Step 9 is natural: $e_F,t_F$ by [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange, def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], $\iota_F$ by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural], the operation comparisons by [lem-fix-operation-reduction], and $a,v$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Composing their naturality squares proves naturality of the displayed equality in $K$, including arbitrary morphisms in the raw rationalization, since the extension on morphisms is the linear scalar localization of the integral extension [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

proof.text: For $E=M$ the specified pull/scalar comparisons are identities [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and $v$ is the identity [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. The proper coefficient comparison is the mate of the identity pull comparison; the open comparison is the identity tensor comparison. The mate formula makes $u,z,\rho$ identities, hence $b=1$ and the equation reduces to $t=t$. For $E\subset M\subset L$, identify the two scalar-extension functors by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The pull comparisons obey its associator by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For the proper comparison, take the counit transpose of $u^{L/M}_{T_{\overline X,M/E}(-)}\,T_{s,L/M}(u^{M/E})$. Apply first the counit mate equation for $u^{L/M}$ and then the one for $u^{M/E}$; the result is $T_{L/E}(\varepsilon_E)$ preceded by the inverse of the composite pull coefficient comparison. Its tower equation identifies this with the transpose of $u^{L/E}$. The mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives equality. For $z$, both maps are the tensor reassociation of open extension, so tensor associativity [lem-fix-operation-reduction] gives equality. Therefore $\rho^{L/E}=\rho^{L/M}T(\rho^{M/E})$ under the scalar associators. Finally $v$ obeys the explicit associator equation of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Substitute these equations in $b=B(\rho)v$: its two-step comparison equals its direct comparison, and pasting the two equations of Step 9 yields the direct one.

proof.text: For composable Frobenius powers use the composition/scalar equation in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] with $h=g_X^r$ and $k=g_X^t$. It identifies the comparison for $L(g_X^{r+t})^*$ with the two comparisons for $Lg_X^{r*}Lg_X^{t*}$ under the specified composition isomorphisms. The same statement asserts associativity, units and arbitrary finite iterations, before realization and after rationalization. Thus the $d_K$ used in Step 9 has exactly the final composition compatibility claimed in the item; this conclusion uses the composition/scalar theorem and is not inferred from its field-tower clause alone.
